ground_truth.unit: percentage points of the monthly hiring probability per percentage point of state unemployment
ground_truth.location: Table 1, Panel B, column (1), PE <= 10 x U. Rate
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Hiring Over the Business Cycle: With and Without Controls"), Panel B, column (1), row PE <= 10 x U. Rate.  Linear probability model (Equation 1 of the paper) of an indicator equal to 100 if the individual is hired in month t — begins a job at a new firm, either from non-employment in month t-1 or, if employed in t-1, reporting a change of employer since last month; new jobs classified as self-employment are not hires — on an indicator for potential experience (age minus years of education minus six) of at most ten years, and the state monthly unemployment rate interacted with each of the two potential-experience groups (at most ten years; more than ten years), with no main effect of the unemployment rate.  Column (1) has no fixed effects.  Sample: the matched monthly CPS panel, January 1994 to September 2016 (pairs of consecutive months matched on administrative IDs and confirmed on sex, race and age, following Madrian and Lefgren; May-August 1995 and month pairs spanning the eight-month sampling break excluded), civilians over 16 with non-missing age and education, all labour-force statuses in t-1.  Weighted by the average of the two months' CPS sampling weights; standard errors clustered by state (51 including DC).  The coefficient is the young workers' hiring response to one percentage point of state unemployment.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Hiring LPMs (Table 1 A/B cols 1 and 4, Table 2 cols 1-4) estimated by WLS on weighted cell means over state x month x demographic cell x PE<=10 x prior labour-force status; all regressors are constant within cells, so point estimates equal person-level WLS; state-clustered SEs not computed/reported.

State (v2gestfips) is missing in the provided data for mid-2014 through 2016 (2.15M person-months); these cannot be matched to the state unemployment rate and are dropped. Sample also restricted to ages 16-80 (age top-coding above 80 varies over time) with non-missing Hispanic origin; resulting N = 16,964,441.

Years of schooling for potential experience imputed from CPS PEEDUCA categories: <1st=0, 1-4=2.5, 5-6=5.5, 7-8=7.5, 9th=9, 10th=10, 11th=11, 12th no diploma=12, HS=12, some college=13, associate=14, BA=16, MA/professional/PhD=18.
The 2 GB yh_data.csv was read with data.table::fread restricted to the 19 needed columns (select=), not loaded in full, because of the sandbox's 4 GB memory cap and 300 s time limit.

Wage regression uses the average of the two months' CPS final weights (earnings weights not in the data); industry/occupation crosswalked to 2002 census codes by code vintage (industry 1990 codes to 2002, 2002 codes 2003-08, 2007 codes 2009-13, 2012 codes 2014+; occupation 1990 codes to 2002, 2002 codes 2003-10, 2010 codes 2011+).
deviations_stdout: hiring LPMs estimated by WLS on weighted cell means (state x month x demographic x PE-group x prior-status); point estimates identical to person-level WLS, clustered SEs not reported

v2gestfips (state) is missing in the data from mid-2014 onward; those person-months cannot be matched to a state unemployment rate and are dropped; sample further restricted to ages 16-80 with non-missing Hispanic origin
years of schooling imputed from CPS education categories (assumed mapping; master's/professional/PhD = 18 years)
cell.notes: Data are pre-matched consecutive-month pairs (unprefixed = t-1, v2 = t). Hired (x100) = employed in t (PEMLR 1-2) and either non-employed in t-1, or employed in t-1 with PUIODP1 = 2 (no longer with last month's employer); new jobs with class of worker self-employed (PEIO1COW 6,7) are not hires. Young = potential experience (age - schooling - 6) <= 10. Demographic FE = sex x white x Hispanic x 7 education levels. Unemployment rate merged by state and month t. Weights = average of PWSSWGT in t-1 and t. Wage sample: new hires with positive, non-allocated (PRWERNAL = 0) weekly earnings deflated to 1994 by the provided CPI, with state, demographic, month-year, occupation and industry FE (N = 118,285). Exploratory attempts: attempt-1 timed the full fread (209 s) and tabulated variables; attempt-2 tested chunked readBin streaming, which was slower and timed out (killed); attempt-3 gathered sample-restriction diagnostics and ran out of memory at the end of its diagnostics. None printed RESULT lines. No claim-comparison attempts were made.
